test_title: PYST 49: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 04 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following states of India has Konkani as a prominently spoken language?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Konkani** is the official language of Goa and is widely spoken by the majority of the state's population.
 
• It is recognized as one of the 22 scheduled languages of India under the **Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The Konkani language has deep cultural and historical significance in Goa, with its roots traced back to early Indo-Aryan languages.
 
• Konkani is written in multiple scripts, including **Devanagari** (official script), Roman, Kannada, and Malayalam, depending on the region.
 
• The Goa, Daman, and Diu Official Language Act, 1987, declared Konkani as the official language of the state of Goa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Assam**

 
 
• Assamese is the most widely spoken language in Assam and is the state's official language.
 
• The Assamese language is an Indo-Aryan language and holds historical and cultural importance in the northeastern region of India.
 
• Other languages spoken in Assam include Bodo (an official language in the Bodoland region), Bengali, and several tribal languages.
 
 
 
• **Tripura**
 
 
• Bengali is the most widely spoken language in Tripura and serves as the official language of the state.
 
• Kokborok, a Tibeto-Burman language, is another prominent language spoken by the indigenous tribal communities in Tripura.
 
• Tripura is linguistically diverse, with smaller tribal languages also being spoken in the region.
 
 
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**
 
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is known for its linguistic diversity, with over 50 distinct languages spoken by various tribes.
 
• English is the official language of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Prominent tribal languages include Nyishi, Apatani, Monpa, Adi, and Mishmi, among others.
